brief: Bear Traps' September 20 letter frames markets at a 1987-style turning point: high-yield bonds near 8% and Treasuries near 5% again offer equity-like returns, which historically preceded the October 1987 crash, and Western debt-to-GDP is now double 1987 levels. The FOMC hiked 25bp Wednesday with a dovish dot plot (one more hike, none in 2027), but Warsh's press conference read hawkish (inflation risks skewed to the upside), and France's budget crisis then blew out the OAT-Bund spread past 100bp, dragging G7 yields including the US lower and undercutting the Fed's effort to control the long end. Credit stress corroborates the bond thesis: convertible debt issuance hit a record $135bn year-to-date (44% AI-related) and CCC spreads widened to 922bp. Equity breadth is the worst in almost 100 years, with the S&P near highs but far more new lows than highs, comparable only to 1973 and 1999. Separately, Hormuz has been closed nearly 200 days, and a veteran commodity investor sees a 5m bpd Atlantic refining shortfall as a right-tail inflation risk.
